articles.title: Shrewsbury Town: Scott Davidson's takeover includes Brad Friedel
articles.summary: Scott Davidson's proposed takeover of League Two club Shrewsbury Town is supported by fellow American Brad Friedel.
articles.body:
Former USA international goalkeeper Brad Friedel has emerged as part of the American group, led by Miami-based Scott Davidson, lining up to take over struggling League Two club Shrewsbury Town.

BBC Shropshire report that the group is fronted by prospective owner Davidson, a 58-year-old American who made his money in real estate. He already has a foot in British football, having been a director of The Spartans, the upwardly mobile Scottish League Two club, since July 2021.

It was confirmed on Monday that Davidson had been cleared by the English Football League and the Independent Football Regulator to proceed with the takeover after passing the owners' and directors' test.

Talks are continuing between both parties in the takeover, which would mark the end of 85-year-old chairman Roland Wycherley's three-decades-long tenure.

The deal, which involves both Davidson and Friedel joining the Shrewsbury board, is expected to be completed within the next few weeks.

Who is Scott Davidson? Analysis from Nick Southall

Shrewsbury fans will no doubt be scouring the internet to discover more about their new owner in waiting, Scott Davidson - but the man supporting him needs no introduction to British football fans.

Friedel, who has played a key supportive role throughout the takeover process, describes Davidson as one of the most talented and humble people he has ever met.

Although not a household name like Friedel, Davidson has his own impressive track record both in business and in the football world - a self-made multi-millionaire with a commercial real estate background.

From studying at the Yale School of Management, he spent 12 years as managing director at New York-based American multinational banking institution JPMorganChase. But, since making his fortune, his love of football has grown.

He's a majority shareholder of Spartans, whose rise since he landed in Edinburgh has been obvious, helping them to win promotion from the Lowland League to within touching distance of the SPFL League One.

His instant success is regarded as one of the biggest success stories in Scottish football over the last couple of years. He's also played a part in developing Spartans' football foundation, regarded as one of the biggest in the UK.

Throw into the mix he's got a UEFA 'A' licence. Why? Because it helps him as an owner to understand exactly what a football manager needs.

A unique level of preparation that Davidson hopes, with Friedel's support, he gets the chance to put into action at Shrewsbury Town.

Ohio-born Friedel has played an active role in helping Davidson during the process of acquiring the club.

He retired at the age of 44 in 2015 after a 20-year senior professional career in which he made 668 appearances, including 476 in the Premier League for Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur.

He was also capped 82 times by the United States and selected in the national squad for three World Cups.

The 55-year-old was in charge of MLS club New England Revolution from 2017-19 and has been working as a pundit for BBC Sport, Talksport, RTE and Fox Sports.

articles.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta says he deliberately disrupted pre-season plans to teach players to adapt
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says Arsenal were ready for their midweek Champions League flight delay - because he deliberately disrupted their training and travel plans in pre-season to prepare them.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal were ready for their midweek Champions League flight delay - because he deliberately disrupted their training and travel plans in pre-season to prepare them.

The Premier League champions were affected by air traffic control issues as they travelled to Italy to face Napoli on Wednesday.

They eventually arrived three hours behind their schedule but manager Arteta said his team were ready because of his methods.

"I love those challenges, I try to create them in pre-season," Arteta said at his news conference on Friday, before Saturday's Premier League trip to Sunderland (20:00 BST).

"So when they happen, we have already experienced them and we are ready.

"Get to the stadium very late, change the routine so the players have to do something else. When it happens, and it can - the flight can be cancelled, or the train is delayed, there is so much traffic, I don't want the players and staff panicking.

"When that happens, adapt to it. We have two or three hours on the plane - can we use it? Play together, spend some time together, sleep.

"But don't complain or use it as an excuse because it's not helpful at all."

Arteta went on to add that his methods also include delaying meals or transport, take different routes to grounds and making the dressing room hotter and more uncomfortable for players.

He said that it reduces the amount of stress and surprise on a matchday when such disruptions occur.

It is not the first instance of Arteta using unusual methods in his team's preparation.

The Spaniard once brought a light bulb into the dressing room while asking his players to be energetic and shine.

On another occasion, he even hired professional pickpockets to attend a team dinner to take phones and wallets from players, which was used as a lesson to teach them to stay alert.

In 2023, he brought a dog named Win into the training ground to boost morale, saying that it was used to represent the team as a family.

He is not opposed to others in the squad using his methods, either - in April, a fire was lit at the club's training ground before they hosted Sporting in the Champions League.

articles.title: Louzán: "España tiene que albergar la final del Mundial, no puede ser de otra manera"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la RFEF recuerda que "el país número 1" en este deporte y sostiene el 55 % de la candidatura
articles.summary: El presidente de la RFEF recuerda que "el país número 1" en este deporte y sostiene el 55 % de la candidatura
articles.body: El presidente de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF), Rafael Louzán, defendió este viernes que España tiene que albergar la final del Mundial de 2030, que organiza con Portugal y Marruecos, porque es "el país número 1" en este deporte y sostiene el 55 % de la candidatura. "Aunque aún no hay ninguna decisión tomada, creo que España es el lugar, porque no puede ser de otra manera. Actualmente, como saben, somos doblemente campeones del mundo (masculino y femenino) y la capacidad organizativa de España para grandes eventos es incuestionable. De ahí que la realidad nos lleve a que no debe haber otro escenario que no sea que España sea sede de la gran final", manifestó Louzán durante un foro organizado por la SER con motivo del centenario de la Federación Interinsular de Las Palmas. El presidente de la RFEF responde de esta manera a su homólogo de la Federación de Marruecos, Fouzi Lekjaa, que este jueves dio por hecho que el partido que proclamará al campeón del mundo de 2030 se disputará en el nuevo estadio de Casablanca, aún en construcción. "La provincia de Benslimán (en la región de Casablanca donde se construye el estadio) es la que tendrá el honor de organizar la final del Mundial de 2030. (...) El que quiera estar en el próximo gobierno no tiene otra opción que desarrollar la provincia", dijo entre aplausos y ovación de los presentes. La FIFA desmintió rápidamente que haya tomado una decisión: "Tal como se comunicó el 5 de agosto de 2026, la FIFA tomará una decisión a su debido tiempo", aseguraron.

articles.title: Arsenal manager Arteta ‘very surprised’ at Jesus blast over Barcelona move
articles.summary: Gabriel Jesus claims he was forced to train alone before Barcelona move, but Arsenal ‘surprised’ by criticism.
articles.body:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said he was “very surprised” by Gabriel Jesus’s claim that he was forced to train alone and was given no information prior to joining Barcelona.

Jesus ended his four-year spell with the Gunners in September and has since made it clear he felt disappointed with the way his exit was handled.

The Brazilian striker said in an interview this week that “out of nowhere they put me to train apart from the group,” adding that “nobody told me nothing” before he signed for Barcelona.

Responding to Jesus’s criticism, Arteta insisted he had spoken to the former Manchester City star about the transfer and had parted on good terms.

“Very surprised, to be fair. Especially because with Gabi (Jesus) I had an individual talk in the dressing room,” he told reporters on Friday.

“I don’t know what words were said; it’s fine. The words that we used were all about gratitude.”

Arteta also came under fire from former Arsenal striker Ian Wright, who recently said he was “uncomfortable” with what he perceived to be a lack of dialogue between the club and Gabriel Martinelli, who moved to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal on September 3.

But Arteta used the presence of Leandro Trossard, who was sold to Besiktas in July, to watch Arsenal’s victory over Chelsea last weekend as an example of the club’s bond with their former players.

“I don’t know, it’s OK. Sometimes I understand that when you have to deliver bad news, or news that people don’t expect, somebody has to be the bad cop. If I have to be, I have to be and I understand,” he said, before the Premier League champions’ trip to Sunderland on Saturday.

“What is important is normally what happens three months or six months later. When Trossard comes, he’s in the dressing room with all of us, the atmosphere and the relationship you have.

“Thank God so far that with all the players that left, at some point the relationship has been really good. I hope this is the same case.”

articles.title: Griezmann, un fichaje de dibujos animados: "Desde los 18 años mi sueño era llegar a la MLS"
articles.standfirst: El ex de Atlético, Barça y Real Sociedad suma ocho goles y tres asistencias con Orlando City
articles.summary: El ex de Atlético, Barça y Real Sociedad suma ocho goles y tres asistencias con Orlando City
articles.body: Fue Jorge Valdano el que definió a Romário como "un jugador de dibujos animados". Ahora es Antoine Griezmann (Macon, 1991) el que, afincado en Orlando, a las puertas del 'Universo Disney', se ha erigido en un fichaje de dibujos animados. A sus 35 años, el ex del Atlético está poniendo 'patas arriba' la Major League Soccer: acumula ocho goles -siete en Liga- y tres asistencias en 12 partidos con Orlando City. Son ya cuatro partidos seguidos marcando. En el triunfo ante Atlanta United (2-3), compartiendo delantera con el argentino Martín Ojeda, volvió a marcar la diferencia con un nuevo doblete: anotó el 1-1 en el 26' al anticiparse para rematar en el primer palo un centro de Joran Gerbet y anotó el 1-3 en el 77' al resolver, mano a mano, una gran pared con Justin Ellis. “Desde los 18 años, mi sueño era llegar a la Major League Soccer. Era importante para mí llegar en buena forma física y mental, y por eso tomé la decisión", aseguró el internacional francés a modo de presentación. Dicho y hecho. Petar Musa (Dallas) y Lionel Messi (Inter Miami) lideran el 'Pichichi' de la MLS con 18 dianas, pero lo cierto es que, desde su debut con Orlando City, el 23 de julio, nadie ha marcado más goles en Liga (7) que Griezmann. No sólo eso. Griezmann se ha convertido en talismán. Siempre que marca... su equipo no pierde: acumula cuatro victorias y un empate en los cinco partidos que el ex de Real Sociedad, Barcelona y Atlético ha visto puerta. Una racha que explica en gran parte la meteórica ascensión experimentada por Orlando City. Ha pasado de ser antepenúltimo antes de Griezmann -apenas sumaba 14 puntos en 15 partidos- a ocupar puestos de 'playoffs': marcha sexto en la Conferencia Este con 31 puntos en 24 encuentros. “Cada partido de liga es importante desde que dimos el salto a los 'playoffs'. El equipo es consciente de ello. El impulso es fundamental en la MLS… Necesitamos mantenerlo para estar entre los cinco primeros, o incluso entre los tres primeros, ése es nuestro objetivo”, admite el centrocampista Joran Gerbet. 'El Principito' aparca las estadísticas individuales y, si cabe, se muestra aún más ambicioso: “Aquí estoy, con muchas ganas, y mi objetivo es ganar un trofeo y hacer feliz a toda la ciudad”. Lo cierto es que, por el momento, no hay quien le pare.

articles.title: Celtic: Boss Martin O'Neill says side given 'timely' police reminder before derby
articles.summary: Celtic players had a visit from Police Scotland on Friday to give them "a timely reminder" about their "general behaviour" in Sunday's Premier Sport Cup quarter-final against city rivals Rangers, manager Martin O'Neill reveals.
articles.body:
Manager Martin O'Neill says Celtic had a visit from Police Scotland on Friday to give them "a timely reminder" about their "general behaviour" in Sunday's Premier Sport Cup quarter-final against city rivals Rangers.

Both Glasgow clubs were last month ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors after last season's quarter-final - won by Celtic after a penalty shootout at Ibrox - was marred by fan disorder.

It will be the first time Celtic have returned there since, although the Scottish champions did host a Scottish Premiership encounter in May, beating Rangers 3-1.

The Scottish Professional Football League recently announced no away fans will attend Old Firm derbies in the league or League Cup this season.

"We had the police come in today, just a little 15-minute meeting to remind us of our behaviour, which I think is a timely reminder," O'Neill revealed.

O'Neill on Baur fitness, police visit & 'strange' setting

Will fan factor work for or against Rangers?

Celtic take confidence & momentum into 'special' derby - Baur

Asked what had been said, the Northern Irishman said: "They didn't mention this, but I would have assumed that one of the things that would be considered is what happens in the field of play, because these things can be taken further.

"You don't want any sort of punch-ups for a start. Secondly, you don't want excessive celebrations, stuff like that.

"But I think it's just the behaviour in the light of what has happened in recent fixtures. I think that the conversation with the police wouldn't have taken place had not recent events been brought up to us."

Celtic have won the latest three derbies since Rangers beat them 3-1 at Celtic Park in the league in January - and are five points ahead in the Premiership after just six games of the new season.

Asked how having no away fans might impact the match, O'Neill added: "I think the games themselves almost take care of themselves in that sense.

"It'll be strange in many aspects not to have any away fans in our area. I always felt as if it would give you a crumb of comfort in some description.

"Nervously looking forward to it, excitedly looking forward to it."

Rangers have come in for some criticism from their own fans for a poor start to the season under new manager Derek McInnes, although the hosts are on a run of four successive victories.

"I suppose if you get in front in the game, that makes them anxious," O'Neill suggested.

"Talking about getting in front and getting in front are two different things. The crowd will be right behind their team, which you would expect.

"We just do our best. We know that we're up against a very fine side. We're up against a crowd that can make a difference. I'd be delighted to be celebrating something in the game."

articles.title: Rangers vs Celtic: Key talking points ahead of first Old Firm clash of season with League Cup semi-final spot at stake
articles.summary: Rangers host Celtic at Ibrox in Sunday's League Cup quarter-final; there will be no away fans after SPFL ruling; Celtic have won all six league games heading into the clash while Rangers have four consecutive Premiership wins after poor start
articles.body:
Rangers host Celtic at Ibrox on Sunday with a Scottish Premiership meeting across the city just seven days later, live on Sky Sports.

While the Hoops have won all six of their league games this season, Rangers have won their last four after a slow start.

There is far more than just bragging rights at stake on Sunday. Rangers have not won silverware since 2024 and Celtic will want to reclaim the only domestic trophy that eluded them last season.

Can McInnes handle the Old Firm pressure?

The last time Derek McInnes came face-to-face with Martin O'Neill was in last season's Premiership title decider, when he suffered an agonising defeat in what would turn out to be his last match as Hearts head coach.

The 55-year-old is no stranger to high-pressure games and has come up against the Hoops 61 times as a manager, winning 10 of them.

He experienced victory in his only Old Firm appearance as a Gers player, but Sunday will be his first taste of the fixture in the dugout.

In contrast, O'Neill is well-versed in leading Celtic in one of the fiercest derbies in football and his record is respectable to say the least.

In his 28 matches against the Gers, the Northern Irishman has won 16.

One of McInnes' decisions will likely be who starts up front in the absence of captain Lawrence Shankland and fellow striker Youssef Chermiti.

Ryan Naderi kept his place for their midweek win against St Mirren as a reward for scoring the winner vs Motherwell after coming on for the injured Shankland.

He played the full game, but it was substitute Bojan Miovski who netted the only goal. Could it bring the former Aberdeen striker into McInnes' starting line-up?

Kevin Kelsy made his first start since his £9m deadline day move from Portland Timbers and will also be in the manager's thoughts. He has yet to find the net in a Rangers top, so would the intensity of an Old Firm clash be the place for him to shine?

O'Neill made five changes for Celtic's midweek win at St Johnstone as he rested some key players ahead of Sunday's clash.

Camilo Duran, who has scored six goals this season, is set to return to the starting XI after the manager admitted they missed him in Perth.

He came on to replace Haissem Hassan and played on the right while Kasper Hogh, returning from injury, was preferred in the central attacking role.

Will O'Neill drop the Dane in favour of Duran through the middle, or will he decide to play them both at Ibrox?

Cameron Carter-Vickers was rested completely in midweek after starting every match so far this season. Dane Murray put in a solid performance in his absence, but will the experience of Carter-Vickers be preferred by O'Neill?

Wolves loanee Sam Johnstone was selected ahead of regular goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo and made a fine save at 0-0.

Given his performance and clean sheet, will O'Neill stick with the England international in the fierce Ibrox atmosphere?

Only Rangers fans are allowed in the 50,000-capacity Ibrox for the League Cup quarter-final against Celtic at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants .

Both clubs had previously agreed that an away ticket allocation of five per cent would be in place for all SPFL games at both grounds.

However, following the on-pitch clashes between fans after their Scottish Cup match in March and an independent review, those arrangements were reconsidered.

The Hoops have been to Govan without any of their own fans before and won, so there will likely not be as big a concern from the Parkhead support this time around.

"I think we've got to bring the crowd with us.

"You're not going to play Celtic and dominate the game for 90 minutes. We'll have spells, they'll have spells, it's just the way it is.

"I think it's important that we tap into having that 50,000 behind us and be behind the players, support them, have their backs, not be on their backs and really make it as tough for Celtic as possible.

"We've got our part to play in that and I felt that if we can capitalise on good play and good opportunities, which we didn't do last night and we didn't do against Motherwell (also won 1-0) obviously, if we can get ourselves in front, give the crowd something to get behind, then I think the strength of our club can be shown.

"I think if the 50,000 can be utilised and we can have the strength of performance in the team that will help the team, it will be difficult to stop."

"Looking forward to it in the usual way, nervously looking forward to it, excitedly looking forward to it. It's a great fixture.

"It'll be strange in many aspects not to have any away fans in our area. I always felt as if it would give you a crumb of comfort in some description, but it is what it is.

"We had police come in today, just a little 15-minute meeting with us, just reminders of our behaviour, which I think is actually a timely reminder, it's a good thing as well.

"I think it's the overall picture. Gosh, it'd be nice to have something to celebrate. I think it's just general behaviour from us.

"The games themselves almost take care of themselves in that sense.

"There's a great atmosphere. The league game that we played, 2-0 down early on in proceedings and Ibrox probably as loud as it's ever been and a really great atmosphere reciprocated by us in the little split game as well too, I thought that was really great.

"But I just think it'll be a bit strange not having the fans in, but as I say, the atmosphere takes care of itself."

articles.title: Man Utd vs Man City: Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are the perfect answer to Rodri's summer exit
articles.summary: In the battle of expensive midfield makeovers, Manchester City's trio look the most complete, with Ayyoub Bouaddi the latest newcomer to impress Enzo Maresca; Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez have also made excellent starts in the wake of Rodri's exit
articles.body:
City did fail to consolidate their advantage until late on, but never really looked in danger of squandering it. Statistically, Porto were restricted to scraps. For a team who had not been beaten at the Estadio do Dragao throughout the whole of 2026, there were few clear-cut chances to speak of. Not a single shot on target.

Man City's superbly balanced midfield made sure of that.

The danger here is of course to compare what City are serving up under Maresca with performances of the past, where everything flowed simultaneously around Rodri in the style of Pep Guardiola. The football so neat and tidy, with every pass in its precise place, it's difficult to pick fault. But that reality has passed.

There remains no rush about Maresca or the implementation of his philosophy. "Slowly, slowly," he urged on Tuesday, keenly aware that most expected Guardiola's departure to shift the balance of power in Manchester. They might well be disappointed.

Beyond surface level, the Porto win offered plenty of reason to believe Man City are building. Away victories in the Champions League should not be sniffed at, much less with a clean sheet attached.

But the individual display of Ayyoub Bouaddi should perhaps be highlighted as the biggest win. Erling Haaland might argue his match-winning double deserved some column inches, but such is the frequency, certain instances can afford to be glossed over in favour of someone else. This is one of them.

Haaland's most perceptive take actually happened post-match. "I told the chairman [Khaldoon Al Mubarak], we've got a gem there," he said of Bouaddi's influence in Porto. "He did a really good game. He's been amazing in training."

The £86m summer signing from Lille possesses a unique brand of confidence for a player still lodged in his teenage years. Not arrogant or showy, just calm and measured. His first Man City start revealed him to be a very accomplished act indeed, with plenty of Rodri-like mannerisms.

"He was never in panic... the performance from him was unbelievable," beamed Maresca on Prime Video.

Bouaddi has obvious belief in his own technical ability. The shimmies and feints to change direction in possession were evidence of that. He has a controlled tempo about his passing. And he's won the early trust of team-mates, too, who were unbothered about giving him the ball under pressure. Rayan Cherki used him as the bounce player all night.

No higher compliment can be paid than highlighting his passing accuracy as being just as judicious as the previous occupier of this role at City. Rodri was pulling the strings for Barcelona in a 5-1 win over Feyenoord 24 hours later, boasting a passing accuracy of 96 per cent. Against Porto, Bouaddi's was 98 per cent.

This small sample size is clearly not enough to consider the youngster directly comparable. "Baby Rodri" was a tag that seemed to suffocate Nico Gonzalez when he was at the club. It sets you up for failure. But it's clear the make-up of Man City's new midfield is capable of making up for the loss of a player that nobody previously thought replaceable.

Individually, Rodri remains one of a kind. Though the Spaniard's limitations in his final few seasons at Man City after suffering an ACL injury in 2024 meant he could not be relied on to play every three days. But with Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez, Maresca has a trio of champion midfielders who can.

Anderson is already putting up possessional numbers comparable with Rodri, which is no surprise given he outperformed the 30-year-old across most metrics while playing for Nottingham Forest last term. He is the hinge holding this plan together.

Add Enzo Fernandez to the mix and Maresca has an enviable blend of talent and tenacity. Not one metronome, but three capable of being just as effective in unison.

Of course that is what £326m should buy you. Anderson came off the bench against Porto and was the picture of control, extremely impressive on and off the ball. He is a safer pair of hands than Bouaddi given relative age and Premier League experience, but the 18-year-old will gain plenty from training and playing alongside him.

The spectrum of profiles at Maresca's aid is important, too. Bouaddi is most naturally a No 6, Anderson and Fernandez conform to a No 8 type. But it's moveable. All three have the mobility and dynamism to cover both positions. Fernandez can even play in the 10 and adds a layer of goal threat previously lacking from midfield. Similar to the role of Ilkay Gundogan under Pep, which has arguably never been filled.

All in all, this revamp is made of promising stuff. And the way each has settled into Maresca's positionally fluid system is the money-can't-buy element. £326m might guarantee individual class but does not come with an assurance of immediate success. Connections often take time. Less applicable here.

The biggest test so far comes at Old Trafford against Man Utd this weekend, live on Sky Sports, with both teams relying on their respective midfield makeovers to establish control in a rivalry that often gets heated.

It's likely Maresca will revert to Anderson in the holding role with Fernandez just ahead. Bouaddi will have a part to play, too, even if that might be from the bench. It's still early days for the club's newest "gem". But he's a prospect that should excite. One who, in time, might even offer every midfield quality imaginable.

Maybe Manchester City do not need Rodri after all.

articles.title: Michail Antonio: Ex-West Ham striker joins Watford
articles.summary: Watford announce the signing of former West Ham United striker Michail Antonio on a free transfer.
articles.body:
Watford have announced the signing of former West Ham United striker Michail Antonio on a free transfer.

The 36-year-old made his final senior appearance for the Hammers in their 3-1 defeat by Leicester City on 3 December 2024, suffering a broken leg four days later in a car crash.

Antonio last played in April for Qatari side Al-Sailiya and made a total of four appearances for the club. He had been training with Alessio Dionisi's Hornets for the past month and has joined on a one-year deal.

"Watford is a big club and hopefully I can come in and bring success and help wherever I can." Antonio told the club's website. , external

The deal for the Jamaican international has been announced pending international clearance that would allow him to be part of the squad for Saturday's Championship home match with Stoke City.

After being released by the Hammers in June 2025 following a 10-year spell, Antonio returned to the club as part of his rehabilitation and played two games for the under-21 side in Premier League 2.

He trained with Leicester City last December and had also been close to a move to Brentford but sustained a torn calf muscle the day before he was set to sign for the Bees, which scuppered the deal.

Prior to his move to West Ham in September 2015, Antonio played in the EFL for clubs including Reading, Sheffield Wednesday and Nottingham Forest.

Antonio, who will wear the number 18 shirt at Vicarage Road, is Watford's 12th signing of the summer.

The Hornets are 12th in the league, having won two, drawn two and lost two of their first six games under Dionisi.

articles.title: Rangers vs Celtic: Martin O'Neill reveals 'general behaviour' message from police ahead of Old Firm League Cup clash
articles.summary: Celtic face Rangers at Ibrox in Sunday's League Cup quarter-final; there will be no away fans after SPFL ruling; Mika Baur is available for the Hoops despite missing training; Martin O'Neill's side have won all six of their Premiership games this season
articles.body:
There will be no Hoops fans in the 50,000-capacity stadium at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants.

The spat is partly a result of the last Old Firm clash in Govan in March, which was marred by fans' disorder as Celtic won the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup quarter-final on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes.

The two clubs have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors and have also been handed a £100,000 compensation bill, paid to whichever team is drawn as the away side in their next respective fixtures in that competition.

The 74-year-old Hoops boss admitted that "it'll be a bit strange not having the (Celtic) fans in but I'm nervously and excitedly looking forward to it; it's a great fixture" and also spoke about the police visit.

O'Neill said: "We had the police come in today, just a little 15-minute meeting with us, just reminders of our behaviour, which I think is actually a timely reminder. It's a good thing as well.

"I think it's the overall picture. Gosh, it'd be nice to have something to celebrate. I think it's just general behaviour from us.

"They didn't mention this but I would have assumed that one of the things that they considered is what happens on the field of play, because these things can be taken further.

"You don't want any sort of punch-ups for a start; secondly, you don't want too excessive celebrations, stuff like that, if that was the case.

"I mean, I'd be delighted to be celebrating something in the game. But it's the behaviour in the light of what has happened in recent fixtures."

O'Neill, who confirmed midfielder Mika Baur will train on Saturday after missing training on Friday with a knock, has yet to decide whether late summer signing Sam Johnstone keeps his place in goal or makes way for Viljami Sinisalo, who started the season as number one.

Experienced England international Johnstone, on loan from EFL Championship club Wolves, made his Hoops debut in the 1-0 Scottish Premiership win over St Johnstone at McDiarmid Park on Wednesday night but O'Neill was coy about the trip to Govan.

He said: "I haven't made my mind up at all. It was a matter of getting a look at what Sam can do.

"It's great to have the two of them. Big Viljami has done exceptionally well for us and it was just, again, an opportunity to see what Sam can do now.

"What he could do a couple of years ago was fantastic; what he can do now might be a totally different picture. I will let them know first."

articles.standfirst: Fernando Gómez Colomer, histórico ex futbolista del Valencia, en Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Fernando Gómez Colomer, histórico ex futbolista del Valencia, en Radio MARCA
articles.body: Fernando Gómez Colomer es una de las figuras más importantes de la historia del Valencia CF. El mítico '10' del conjunto 'ché', se pasó por 'El Programa de Ortega' para celebrar un cumpleaños marcado por la complicada realidad que vive el valencianismo. "Sí que estoy preocupado porque otros años, que han sido parecidos en los comienzos, lo hemos pasado mal pero siempre pensábamos que al final se reaccionaría. Pasó con Baraja y Corberán cuando llegaron. Lo malo no son solo los resultados es que las sensaciones no son muy buenas y el jugador empieza a estar un poco apático y desesperado y no rinde como quizá podría", afirmó. Fernando se mostró muy claro y contundente al hablar de la situación que vive el club provocada por las malas decisiones de sus dirigentes, que hace siete años, despedían a Marcelino tras haber ganado una Copa del Rey y logrado dos clasificaciones consecutivas para Champions. Un horizonte que hoy parece muy lejano. "Todos pensábamos en la llegada de un máximo accionista que se hacía cargo de un club con muchos problemas económicos y pensábamos que habría una inversión importante y que el equipo se podría recuperar algo de dónde estaba. Marcelino fue campeón de Copa y dos años en Champions. El profesional que llega aquí se da cuenta de que tiene que hacer su trabajo, quizá públicamente exigir y levantar la voz lo menos posible porque a todos les ha pasado que cuando han levantado un poquito la voz, han sido destituidos. Es una pena porque se acabó la inversión y el beneficio y comenzaron los problemas sociales, económicos y deportivos. Hace mucho tiempo que debían de haber dejado de ser máximos accionistas del Valencia porque ya no hay nada. Estamos cada vez peor y las cosas no parecen tener una solución definitiva y clara", apuntó. La delicada situación del club en lo deportivo tiene en el punto de mira a Carlos Corberán que, pese a haber renovado en verano por dos campañas, vive unas horas decisivas en el banquillo si no llegan buenos resultados. El conjunto valencianista es colista tras las 4 primeras jornadas. "Siempre ha tenido mucho apoyo por parte del club. A mí no me gusta que los entrenadores sean destituidos pero el fútbol está montado así. Además de los resultados, las sensaciones no son buenas, se ve al equipo apático, como dejándose un poco ir, cuando las cosas no salen...creo que estos 2 o 3 próximos partidos pueden marcar un poco, pero filtrar que hay un ultimatum... es una de las noticias más perjudiciales para tu equipo", comentó. Las últimas horas en Valencia también han estado marcadas por las palabras de Rodri en el banquillo durante el Valencia-FC Barcelona en el que afirmaba que los jugadores de Corberán "eran malísimos", unas palabras de las que el capitán de la selección ya se ha disculpado y que entiende, en parte, Fernando Gómez Colomer. "Él no lo hace ni por criticar ni por hablar mal de tus compañeros, pero ese comentario es mejor hacerlo tapándote la boca o dentro del vestuario porque al final el "Estos son malísimos" pues estás hablando de otro jugador de otro equipo. Se entienden las disculpas, se entiende que no es una crítica, pero al final estás hablando de jugadores del Valencia. Aquí han gustado mucho esas declaraciones porque los aficionados creen que dice la verdad, pero hay cosas que es mejor hablarlas en privado. Lo entendemos, lo disculpamos pero hubiese sido mejor que no se hubiera producido".

articles.title: Inaki Williams: Athletic Club forward retires from Ghana duty
articles.summary: Inaki Williams says the time has come to bring his journey with the Black Stars to an end four years after making his international debut.
articles.body:
Athletic Club forward Inaki Williams has announced his retirement from international duty with Ghana.

The 32-year-old scored two goals in 28 caps for the Black Stars after making his debut in September 2022.

He featured for the West Africans at the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups and the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon).

Williams appeared twice at this year's World Cup as Ghana were knocked out in the last 32 by Colombia.

"I feel the time has come to bring my journey with the Ghana national team to an end," he said in a post on social media.

"I leave happy, proud and with the peace of mind of knowing that I gave everything every time I wore this shirt."

Williams, who was born in Bilbao to Ghanaian parents, chose to represent the Black Stars after previously playing for Spain at youth level and in a 2016 friendly at senior level.

His younger brother Nico, who also plays for Athletic Club in Bilbao, chose to represent Spain and has gone on to become a World Cup and European Championship winner with La Roja.

Inaki Williams' announcement comes a week after it was confirmed that Carlos Queiroz would return as Ghana coach in the build-up to the 2027 Afcon in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

He said his time with Ghana had given him "much more than football".

"It has allowed me to come back home, feel even closer to my roots and experience the enormous pride of representing my country and wearing this flag on my chest," he added.

"Thank you from the bottom of my heart to everyone who has been part of this journey and for all the love you have always shown me.

"Ghana will always be a part of me. I will continue supporting the Black Stars as one of you, wherever I am."

articles.title: Mourinho: Vinicius Jr and Kylian Mbappé are ‘trees that bear fruit’
articles.summary: José Mourinho has defended Kylian Mbappé and Vinicius Junior amid jeers from Real Madrid fans by using a Portuguese proverb about fruit trees. Los Blancos’ p...
articles.body:
José Mourinho has defended Kylian Mbappé and Vinicius Junior amid jeers from Real Madrid fans by using a Portuguese proverb about fruit trees.

Los Blancos' promising start to the Portuguese's second spell in charge continued with Tuesday's 2-1 win against Italian champions Inter Milan.

But the Champions League opener was overshadowed somewhat by Real fans expressing dissatisfaction with stars Mbappé and Vinicius in the Bernabéu win.

Mourinho's side will again play at home on Saturday when they face Rayo Vallecano in La Liga and the veteran head coach has defended the pair in the build-up.

"In Portugal, there is a proverb that I don't know if it exists in Spain: you only throw stones at trees that bear fruit," the Real boss said of Brazil international Vinicius.

"What has Vini Jr done here in recent years? How many Champions Leagues has he won, and how many goals has he scored? What has he done here in the last five or six years?

"He is a tree that bears a lot of fruit, and people throw stones because they want the fruit. They want the best of Vinicius, and the best will come.

"Against Benfica, he single-handedly decided the tie. That Vinicius will come, but at this moment, he hasn't been at that level yet.

"This is a Vini who is working harder than ever. In this era of data, he is very close to his top speed. He broke his record this season in terms of balls recovered and also in the defensive third… he will arrive soon."

Mourinho is as demanding as anyone – something he noted, referencing comments made by defender Dean Huijsen – and leant on the same Portuguese adage when talking about Mbappé.

"I don't talk about who criticizes," he said. "I use the same proverb as for Vini because he is a tree with plenty of fruit.

"I can comment on his statements, and he's right. A player with over 40 goals is never a problem for the team. When there is empathy, friendship, commitment, and respect, imagine that… then there are things I see and value greatly as a coach.

"Some people don't understand, and that's normal. Some people don't know football in depth. Others understand football in depth but find it convenient not to talk about good things.

"I've seen a team play after the 90th minute with 10 players and Mbappé on the left wing, ahead of (Marc) Cucurella , who was exhausted, with Mbappé also exhausted, defending like an animal and with a very demanding coach who wouldn't stop shouting and motivating.

"I value this absolutely incredibly. It's a joy to see this kind of behaviour. There are people who know as much about football as I do, who have also seen it and don't say it.

"They say we didn't defend well and could have conceded three or four goals. But they don't say we could have scored eight."

articles.title: El Barça, el equipo más rematador de LaLiga
articles.standfirst: En los cuatro primeros encuentros ha realizado 84 disparos
articles.summary: En los cuatro primeros encuentros ha realizado 84 disparos
articles.body: El Barcelona es el equipo más ofensivo de LaLiga. Además de sumar ya, en solo cuatro jornadas disputadas 17 goles y liderar este apartado, también reina en número de remates totales. Los culés han tenido 84 ocasiones. Únicamente el Real Madrid le sigue de cerca, aunque con menos acierto. Los merengues ha disparo 80 veces y han logrado 10 dianas. La diferencia entre ambos grandes, sin embargo, es mucho mayor cuando se pone el foco en la efectividad. Mientras el Barcelona ha celebrado 17 goles en este arranque de campeonato, el Real Madrid suma 10. El Atlético de Madrid aparece como tercer equipo con más remates, con 70 lanzamientos, aunque ya bastante lejos de los dos grandes. Los culés están viviendo un inicio de temporada espectacular. Sus números cara a puerta son letales. Pese al debate durante todo el verano de la llegada del '9', los catalanes han demostrado que Hansi Flick tiene muchas alternativas en la plantilla. En las cuatro primera jornadas, los azulgranas ya han rematado un total de 84 veces. Contra el Athletic, los culés dispusieron de 22 ocasiones; en Elche, 11; contra el Rayo, 26; y en Valencia, 25. Por lo tanto, únicamente en el Martínez Valero, los catalanes tiraron de efectividad para llevarse la victoria. El único equipo de LaLiga que les sigue el ritmo es el Real Madrid, pero con menos acierto. Los merengues han disparado un total de 80 ocasiones en las cuatro jornadas y han celebrado siete goles menos que el Barcelona. En el lado totalmente opuesto está el Dépor. Pese a su buen momento en la clasificación, solo ha generado 33 oportunidades, el Celta atesora 35 y el Getafe, 39. El buen momento ofensivo del Barcelona no se limita al campeonato regular. Si se amplía la estadística de remates por partido a la máxima competición europea, los azulgranas también aparecen entre los equipos que más veces han buscado la portería rival en la jornada inaugural. Después del primer cruce, el Barcelona ocupa la quinta posición en número de disparos, con 22. Solo cuatro equipos han rematado más: el PSG, que lidera la estadística con 35; Arsenal y Lens, ambos con 26; y el Bayern de Múnich, con 25. El Real Madrid, por su parte, realizó 16 remates en su enfrentamiento contra el Inter.

articles.title: Man Utd vs Man City: Kings of Manchester hotly debated ahead of Old Trafford derby showdown
articles.summary: Elliot Anderson called Manchester City the 'Kings of Manchester' but will United dethrone their local rivals at Old Trafford this weekend? Watch Man Utd vs Man City live on Sky Sports from 4pm on Sunday; kick-off 4.30pm.
articles.body:
That coronation came from City's £116m summer signing Elliot Anderson - and has been hotly debated in the build-up to the Manchester derby Super Sunday showdown at Old Trafford, which you can watch live on Sky Sports.

Is Anderson right? Does City's huge recent success mean they rule the roost? Or are Manchester United still No 1?

Anderson was asked about the Manchester derby during an interview with Manchester City's official club website this summer.

"It's one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester," Anderson said.

"It'll be a great fixture and I can't wait to be involved in something like that."

Maresca 'excited' by 'special' Manchester derby

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says Anderson's verdict rings true in recent years.

"Probably the reason why Elliot said that was that he grew up in the last 15 years, Manchester City were unbelievable with what they achieved. It's normal Elliot said that," said Maresca.

"If you go back, then it's a different picture but when he grew up Manchester City were dominant."

Speaking in an interview with Sky Sports , Maresca outlined the importance of these Manchester match-ups to all involved.

"It's special because it's two teams in the same city. It's special for the fans, the club, for everyone," said Maresca.

"I'm very excited. These are the games I like. These are the games we want. We know it's going to be a tough game. Since Michael [Carrick] took over they're doing a fantastic job. We can show respect in the derby by trying to be ourself and go there to try to win."

Michael Carrick was a Manchester United player when City were labelled "noisy neighbours" by former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in 2009. But the current United head coach says City's subsequent Premier League wins and triumphs in the derby have ramped up the rivalry.

Speaking to Sky Sports , Carrick said: "When I first came to the club, to be honest, it wasn't like it is now.

"In 20 years, it's kind of grown, it's developed, it's changed a little bit over the years."

Carrick pinpoints Vincent Kompany's derby winner in April 2012 - a month before City's last-day Premier League title triumph - as a key moment in the duel for supremacy in Manchester.

"The one where we ended up losing the league, when Kompany scored the header towards the end of the season. We had a bit of a lead and then we lost it, and then we lost it at the end of the season. That felt quite a big moment," he said.

"That's just the one that we lost, so it probably hurts. We always remember those ones the most."

There have been glorious derby days for United, too, which Carrick remembers more fondly.

"Probably the [2010 League Cup] semi-final is up there, when we won late and I scored and Wayne [Rooney] scored a header. That was a good day.

"Robin [Van Persie] scoring in the last minute [in the Premier League win at the Etihad in December 2012] the last time we won the league.

"When Michael [Owen] scored that one at the Stratford End [in September 2009]."

"Wayne's overhead kick in 2011? I forgot about that one! That was a special one."

Carrick is now hoping to add to that list. "There were some really good games over the years, hopefully we can come out on top on Sunday."

Manchester United have got the Manchester derby - and their season is in the balance too. If you beat Manchester City, you're flying. If you get beat by Manchester City, here we go again.

It would be one point from two games including the Everton game. And other teams are winning around you.

So I am worried - and this is why I didn't put Manchester United in my top five at the start of the season. Nothing's changed for me since then. When you draw games, it hurts you.

shree: City have won a lot recently and you know it's all because of oil money and a world class coach. United haven't been best in recent years but the point we are still doing this comparison itself shows how great a club Manchester United are which City won't be able to be.

Argyle loyal: At this moment in time it's definitely City, the days of United being kings of Manchester went when Fergie left.

Aaron s: I think it has to be Man U. Look at their history. Man U just played and won their 300th Champions League game. Look at the amount of trophies they have won compared to Manchester City. City may have become bigger recently but Man U are and will always be the kings of Manchester.

PeteUK: Remember when United fans jumped on Liverpool fans for 'living in the past'? How the tables have dramatically turned, United are Kings like Arthur: relegated to history books.

Woop: I think City are the better side and have been over the last 15 years but Manchester United are a bigger football club. I don't see United winning a league for a long time though whereas city will.

Shanepancho778: As a lifelong Liverpool fan it's nice to finally say that Manchester is definitely blue and will be for the foreseeable future. Those glory days left in 2013 when Ferguson retired.
